mappings.note: The 'Era of the Books' speech is the Historian's museum frame talking, which is what LO-7 covers, and its content is the value of reading.
The Martians. Extraction.
Hats, sandwiches, secret codes: the misreading of the Mother Goose volume, itemised. LO-8.
Correcting the chief while flattering him is how the play makes arrogance ridiculous. Not LO-8: the joke here is Think-Tank's vanity, not the book.
Asks the student to handle the same vanity, so the satire of arrogance is what is being tested.
Books against electronic media is the value of reading argued outside the play. Not LO-7: nothing about structure.
Books as a best companion plus a paragraph on a favourite book: the central message, in the written form LO-3 measures.
The misreading of the nursery rhymes as threats, extended to the student's own misunderstandings. LO-8.
Aliens who happen to speak English is a convention of the genre, which is exactly what LO-6 asks to be named. Not LO-4, since the question is about the form rather than the setting.
The year 2040. Extraction.
The twentieth century. Extraction.
Think-Tank. Extraction.
Iota is the lieutenant. Extraction -- and the item that the later rank question contradicts.
'Ridiculous little planet' is Think-Tank's contempt in his own words. The satire of arrogance, not a location fact.
Reading a public library as a crude refreshment stand is the misreading at its broadest. LO-8.
Oop tasted it. Extraction.
Noodle's guess that the 'sandwich' is a communication device is the misreading half-corrected. LO-8.
'Eye communication' is the play's comic route from sandwich to reading. LO-8.
All three inferences from the Humpty Dumpty picture are the same misreading. Not LO-1, since the key is 'all of the above'.
That nursery rhymes saved the planet IS the play's message about reading, as an MCQ.
Books mistaken for sandwiches. The founding misreading.
That books were for eating. LO-8.
Noodle's first guess, hearing. Part of the same comic sequence.
Noodle's second guess, reading -- where the misreading finally lands on the truth.
From Mars. Extraction.

Mapped to the framing outcome because the twenty-fifth century is the Historian's vantage point, not the date of the invasion. NOTE the inconsistency: two other items in this chapter place the invasion in the twenty-first century and one dates it to 2040, so a student meeting all three gets contradictory answers.
Mother Goose named as the book that saved the Earth. LO-23's illustration.
Marsopolis. Extraction.
Martians. Extraction.
Oop's hat guess. One of the misreadings.
Swallowing vitamins in order to read is an invented mechanic of the play's world, which is what LO-6's 'conventions of the genre' means here.
The cow that jumped over the moon read as a flying animal. LO-8.

Mapped as extraction of Iota's rank. DEFECT of the known letter-versus-value kind: the item is keyed to option D while the model answer reads '(c) Commander'. It is also wrong on the facts -- another item in this same chapter has Iota as the lieutenant, which is option C's text.
Two moons. Extraction.
Think-Tank ruled Mars. Extraction.
Sandwiches, then ear devices, then eye devices -- the whole misreading sequence in one option. LO-8.
'Great and Mighty' is the title he awards himself, which is the satire in a phrase. Not LO-1.
Claire Boiko. Extraction.
Oop is the sergeant. Extraction.
Omega is the captain. Extraction.
A book of nursery rhymes against a science book, an encyclopedia and a military manual: the message is that the humblest book did it.
Noodle is the deputy. Extraction.
The Martians. Extraction, the MCQ twin of the short answer.
'The Era of the Book'. Extraction of the label.
Omega, Iota and Oop. Extraction of the crew list.
The play's twenty-fifth century setting is the museum frame LO-7 names.
Noodle replacing Think-Tank is the satire's payoff -- the flatterer outlasts the boaster. Not LO-1: the substitution is the joke.
Think-Tank calling off the invasion is the Martians' defeat, which is LO-23's illustration.
Asks for a comment on nursery rhymes saving the world. The core LO-23 item.
The Mistress Mary rhyme read as agriculture combined with mining. LO-8's misreading, explained.
Defines satire in the stem and asks the student to show it in the play. LO-9 outright.
The flight to Alpha Centauri follows directly from the misread rhymes, so the defeat and the misreading are both in play.
Animals taught music and space travel: the rhymes read as an intelligence report. LO-8.
What happened in the twenty-fifth century is only knowable from the frame narration, which is what LO-7 asks about.
How the book changed his view of Earth: the book's power, produced entirely by his misreading of it.
Humpty Dumpty's fall read as the fall of Mars. LO-8.
The comparison of races and the sneer 'primitive ball of mud' are the arrogance the play satirises.
Oop chewing a book and finding it dry as Martian dust is the misreading acted out, and the laugh in it.
Noodle's tactful correction about the 'sandwiches'. The misreading being unpicked.
The Historian's praise of books is the message, delivered by the framing device.
Asks what we learn about Iota as a person -- confused, sly enough to make Oop eat first. Character.
'Hey diddle diddle' read as a report on space-trained animals. LO-8.
The large colourful volume, Mother Goose. Extraction.
Seeing his own 'Great and Mighty Balloon Brain' in a Humpty Dumpty illustration is the arrogance punctured and the misreading at once.
Alarm at crops of rare metals and explosives. The third misread rhyme.
Probe One was sent for information before the invasion. Extraction of the plot.
'Weak, ignorant, uncivilised' is his contempt, and the order to the probe follows from it. The satire of arrogance.
Who Omega is, is extraction; why he tried to eat the book is the misreading he was ordered to act on.
Books as companions, and the book that saved the Earth. LO-23 in both halves.
Noodle steering his chief without contradicting him, at five marks. The satire of the vain commander, in extended form.
How the book of rhymes saved the Earth, framed by the wrongness of invasion. LO-23 at five marks.
Three alternative stems: the guesses about the book, and Noodle's handling of the chief. The misreading and the satire together, at length.
All three rhymes and how each frightened him. LO-8's fullest form.
A character sketch of Think-Tank is inseparable from the satire of his arrogance, so both, plus the long-answer form.
Justifying the title means arguing that a book saved the Earth -- LO-23 by another route. Not LO-7: the frame is not in question.
How the crew 'decoded' Mother Goose is the misreading narrated step by step, at five marks.
What he believed Earthlings could grow, and his reaction: the Mistress Mary misreading, extended.
'Pride has a fall' applied to his reaction to the rhymes: the arrogance satirised, by way of the misreading that undoes him.
A character sketch of Noodle and the values he shows. Character, not LO-9: Noodle is the satire's instrument, not its target.
The extract is the 'listen to them' exchange -- the misreading staged -- and the sub-items also retrieve the library setting and Think-Tank's description from it.
